result.summary: The page is mostly well-formed, but the promotional banner has a serious contrast problem: white headline and subtext on a pale green background is barely legible. Other elements (header, chips, carousels, bottom nav) appear intact; the partially visible carousel item at the right edge and the card cut off at the bottom are expected scroll behaviors and not counted as defects.

issues.description: In the '3 free deliveries for you' promo banner, the white heading and the 'Use code TALLINN3 at checkout · min. order €10' subtext sit on a very light mint-green background, resulting in extremely low text contrast that is hard to read and fails WCAG contrast requirements.
issues.suggestion: Darken the banner background (e.g., deep green) or switch the text to a dark color so headline and body text meet at least 4.5:1 contrast against the background.

issues.description: The promo banner's 'Order now' button uses green text on a white pill, which is fine, but the banner's pale background makes the whole banner look washed out / unintentionally disabled compared to the rest of the high-contrast UI.
issues.suggestion: Increase the banner's background saturation or add a border/shadow so the promotional block reads as an intentional, active element.
